reporting-org.narrative: Norad - Norwegian Agency for Development Cooperation

description.narrative:
Norad supports the IEA’s Clean Energy Transitions Programme, which works to strengthen the capacity of developing and middle-income countries to implement their energy transition plans. The programme’s activities include data and analytical work, technical cooperation, policy advice, training, and strategic political dialogue. It has an increasing focus on capacity building to help countries develop frameworks that facilitate energy transition while improving the lives and welfare of their populations. The overarching goal of the programme is to increase access to energy, both in light of the SDGs and the target of net zero emissions by 2050. It aims to build capacity within governments in over 20 selected countries globally, with a particular focus on countries in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA).
The main activities in the new phase (2025–2029) are structured around three pillars:
Access to clean energy, including efforts to promote clean cooking solutions in SSA. Improved coordination of multilateral support to SSA. Making data, analyses, and reports available to support countries in decision-making related to energy transition processes.
The pillars (initiatives) have the following sub-goals:
1) Regional cooperation to increase access to clean cooking energy in Africa, especially through the development of national strategies and policy work for clean cookstoves.
2) Measures to increase investments that can trigger larger and more sustainable efforts to improve energy access.
3) Sector-specific guidance on financing, increased knowledge of carbon credits, and opportunities to expand the use of carbon credits as financing in the cookstove sector. A strengthened framework for carbon financing will help increase the likelihood of private investment. 4) Governance: strengthening institutions in 20+ countries, and building capacity within public administration so that countries are able to meet their own energy transition goals.
